::: {#rem-reading-implies}
#### Reading an implication

An implication with a false premise, as in @exr-false-premise,
is sometimes called *vacuously true*.
Three habits help with implications that sound strange:

- Apply the definition (@def-implies) rather than intuition about the sentence.
- Read $P \Rightarrow Q$ as a promise, as in @exr-broken-promise.
- Look at the cases where $P$ is true;
  they are the only cases where $P \Rightarrow Q$ can be false.

:::
